clue.text: European runs round clubs after swell exotic performer

indicators.note: the dancing part of the answer is placed after the swelling part

parts.note: to swell is to belly out, as a sail does

indicators.note: the European and the runs go round the clubs, enclosing them

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tale of some European bulging round the middle at a nightclub, mistaken for an exotic act.
explanation.definitionFit: A belly dancer is a performer of a Middle Eastern dance style that many audiences find exotic.

clue.text: Statesman wants nothing, as it happens, to appear briefly in court

indicators.note: something that appears in a place shows up inside it, so these words help say one piece goes within another
the nothing plus the shortened broadcast word sit inside the court word

parts.note: the bar is the court of law, as in being called to the bar
O is the zero shape standing for nothing

indicators.note: a word said briefly loses its final letter, here the E

parts.note: a broadcast that goes out as it happens is live

explanation.surface: A politician who wants nothing more than to make a brief court appearance as events unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear ... in' is the container signal, split around 'briefly', which trims the final E. Simón Bolívar liberated much of South America from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Simón Bolívar was the South American liberator and political leader, hence a statesman.

clue.text: Breather before battle's final thrust

indicators.note: the organ comes before the letter taken from the battle

parts.note: a lung is an organ that breathes, so a breather

indicators.note: the final letter of the word battle's is wanted (ignoring the possessive)

explanation.surface: A soldier takes a breather before a battle's last push.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing.

clue.text: Old leader isn't half likely to be blotto

indicators.note: blotto means very drunk, so the letters stagger about into a new order
half of the word likely is taken, its second three letters

explanation.surface: A former leader is quite likely to be drunk, a nod to a notoriously bibulous president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes ELY from 'likely'; with ISNT those letters are rearranged. The surface teases Boris Yeltsin's well-known drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of Russia, a former national leader.

clue.text: Small boy, one month old, showing a certain style

parts.note: Art is a short form of the boy's name Arthur
Dec is the abbreviation for December, one month

explanation.surface: A little boy aged one month is already showing a particular style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 30s, so a particular style.

clue.text: Conservative leading up-to-date revolutionary takeover

indicators.note: the Conservative abbreviation leads, standing in front
something revolutionary turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory at the head of a modern, radical seizure of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is the sudden seizure of government by force, an illegitimate takeover of power.

clue.text: Spaniard's brace riding up in jumper

indicators.note: the bracing word goes inside the jumping animal

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: in a down entry, riding up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to gird is to brace oneself

explanation.surface: A Spanish man's braces ride up inside his sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater but is the kangaroo. Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquín Rodrigo, composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez, was a native of Spain.

clue.text: Officer: extremely effectual …

parts.note: the printed punctuation mark is a colon

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the word effectual

explanation.surface: A list heading: an officer described as supremely effective, continued into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'Officer' is not just punctuation: it is the piece COLON. The ellipsis links this clue's surface to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior commissioned army officer, ranking above lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Cautious course, one I altered to head off mere guesswork

indicators.note: altered to means one letter is changed into the pieces that follow

parts.note: a circuit is a racecourse
one of the two I letters in the course word is the one changed

indicators.note: head off takes the head, the first letter, of the word mere

parts.note: spec, short for speculation, is guesswork

explanation.surface: A cautious route that swaps certainty for mere guesswork.
explanation.walkthrough: The second I of CIRCUIT becomes M (the head of 'mere') plus SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumspect means wary and careful, unwilling to take risks, hence cautious.

clue.text: … crack invader of old, in time, repelled Soviet Russian?

indicators.note: the invader sits inside the time letter and the reversed colour
repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Red was a Soviet communist
the Huns invaded Europe in late antiquity

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: a crack officer from history, an ancient invader, driving off a Soviet in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' reads as an adjective carried over from 'Officer' in 7, but here it is the noun for a sharp noise; 'repelled' turns the colour back and 'in' sets the invader inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack of thunder is the loud report of a storm, so the noun names that sharp sound.

clue.text: Flash car having stop light raised in accordance with fast race

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, a flashy car

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: red is the traffic light that means stop
by means according to, as in by the rules

explanation.surface: A showy car sits at a red light that is lifted up, ready for a high-speed race.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller derby is a fast-moving contact sport raced around a track on roller skates.

clue.text: Show regret, covering over bare back

indicators.note: the regret word covers, enclosing, the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: back means the stripped word is read in reverse
bare strips the word over of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A performance about regretting having one's naked back on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bare back' looks like a naked back, but 'bare' strips the outer letters off 'over' and 'back' reverses what is left; 'covering' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Source exercise in a 'rowing' machine?

parts.note: a seed is the source from which something grows
a drill is a practice exercise

explanation.surface: Where to get an exercise on a gym rowing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'rowing' warn that this is not the gym machine: it is one that sets seeds in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed drill is a farm machine that sows seeds in straight rows, so it puts things in rows.

clue.text: Peacekeepers containing force mutinied?

indicators.note: the peacekeepers contain, holding inside, the forcing word

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops who held back a force that might have turned on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers have risen up in revolt, so the past participle meaning risen up fits, hence the question mark.

clue.text: London street proverb about poor Oliver

indicators.note: the proverb goes about, surrounding, the rearranged name

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in bad shape and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A wise saying about poor Oliver Twist, set in Dickensian London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals the anagram and 'about' the container; the street is famous for bespoke tailoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row is a London street in Mayfair famous for bespoke tailoring.

clue.text: Issue published by company taking on yours truly

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
yours truly is the speaker referring to themselves, me

explanation.surface: A magazine issue brought out by a firm that has hired the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue in the sense of a result or consequence is an outcome.

clue.text: Contract split finds mum left on the outside

indicators.note: the quiet word and the left letter stand on the outside, enclosing the split

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A broken contract leaves Mum out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun about a deal but is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to wrinkle and shrink, which is to contract.

clue.text: Plan again, given hand without a trick

indicators.note: without means the word for hand goes without the letter a

parts.note: to reach someone something is to hand it to them
art is cunning or a trick, as in arts and wiles

explanation.surface: A card player rethinks after being dealt a hand that won no trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' drops the A from REACH, leaving RECH.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart a course is to plan it, so doing it once more is planning again.

clue.text: Books in fiction regularly trash feminists

indicators.note: the books go inside the fiction word

parts.note: a lie is a fiction or falsehood
B is an abbreviation for book, so two of them for books

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word trash

explanation.surface: Books in a fiction series routinely rubbish feminists.
explanation.definitionFit: Libbers is informal shorthand for women's liberationists, feminist campaigners.

clue.text: Booted out after finally pressing to retire

indicators.note: the rearranged footwear word comes after the final letter
finally takes the final letter of the word pressing
out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Kicked out after making one last pressing demand, so off to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night means to turn in and sleep, the idiom for going up to sleep.

clue.text: Fish carried by north European river

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
something on a vehicle is carried by it

explanation.surface: A fish being carried along by a north European river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garonne is a major river of south-west France flowing through Toulouse and Bordeaux.

clue.text: Spirit served by bar on Shetland, say, that's closing early

indicators.note: in a down entry the bar word sits on top of the animal

parts.note: to ban is to bar or forbid

indicators.note: the word stops one letter early, losing its last letter

parts.note: the Shetland is a breed of sheep, so an example of one

explanation.surface: Whisky served in a bar on the Shetland islands, which shuts early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shetland' looks like the islands or the pony; here it is a sheep breed. SHEEP closes early as SHEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is a wailing female spirit of Irish folklore who foretells a death.

clue.text: Well-known brand set in stone

parts.note: brand is an old word for a sword, and the famous one was fixed in a stone until Arthur drew it out

explanation.walkthrough: 'brand' suggests a trade name, but it is a poetic word for a sword; 'set in stone' is literal, not the idiom for fixed rules.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's legendary sword was pulled from a stone, making it the most famous blade ever lodged in rock.

clue.text: Type of screen separately taken from 8 for one fixing keyboards?

indicators.note: the two letters are taken out of the other answer apart from each other, not as one block

parts.note: 8 refers to the solution of 8 across
HD, high definition, is a type of television screen

explanation.surface: A screen type, taken apart from clue 8, as a repair for keyboards.
explanation.walkthrough: H and D come out of the 8-across answer at separate places, leaving TUNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner adjusts the strings of keyboard instruments so they play in pitch.

clue.text: Best businessman in America

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat them, as a winning card beats the others
Donald, the American property tycoon later president

explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to outdo or beat, and Donald Trump is a famous US property tycoon.

clue.text: Plays with wife, at last, when husband is out getting plant

indicators.note: the last letter of wife is put with the reduced word, after it
the husband is out, meaning his letter is removed

parts.note: theatre is the art form of plays

indicators.note: at last takes the last letter of the word wife

explanation.surface: A wife goes to the theatre at last once her husband is away, and comes home with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' removes H from THEATRE to leave TEATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea tree is an Australasian shrub known for its medicinal oil.

clue.text: City in which anything old appears not good

indicators.note: the city has the archaic word set in it

parts.note: NY, New York, is the city
aught is an archaic word for anything

explanation.surface: A city where anything old is seen as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: AUGHT is old-fashioned English for 'anything', as in 'for aught I know'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughty child is badly behaved, which is the opposite of being good.

clue.text: Postpone travelling round with the Parisian urbanites

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the with abbreviation
travelling letters move around into a new order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: City folk delaying a journey to Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges the letters as TONSPEOP, and 'round' puts them around the abbreviation for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Townspeople are the residents of a town, and urbanites are dwellers in towns and cities.
